reformulation: Solver-blind exact reformulation of test18 (MPS NAME test18: 20,617 vars in [0,1], 2,150 integer, 2,147 rows) into the committed output/reformulated.mps: saturation proves z=x for all 18,467 continuous edge coordinates, the 1,000 objective-bearing Y binaries are replaced by their incident-X sums (packing rows), the 4 zero-cost budget-only binaries are deleted, and the 1,000 packing rows reduce to the 928 inclusion-maximal ones. Target: 1,146 binary vars, 929 rows, 18,711 nonzeros (94.4% of columns removed); Optimal -17783 on both sides. Kernel certificate: source.mcm 1,734,649 B, target.mcm 446,645 B, request.json 41,769 B, proof.rpa 39,845,824 B, proof.rpx 30,500,427 B, status VERIFIED.
claim_class: Non-injective projected equivalence plus strict LP separation: three directional claims over the same 1,146 retained coordinates (integer forward, integer reverse, LP reverse) with objective 'Equal', plus one supplementary FiberStrictness point asserting strict containment of the target LP image in the projected source LP image. Projection is non-injective because the four removed budget-only binaries are set to zero in the canonical extension; no LP objective-bound improvement is claimed.
claims: Claim 0 (forward, integrality true both sides): total map from source to the 1,146 retained X coordinates; 5,514 terminal obligations = 1,146 lower + 1,146 upper bounds, 1,146 VarInt facts, 929 target rows, the objective relation and the 1,146 projection identities (cases/test18/preparation.json:30-34).

Claims 1 and 2 (reverse, target to source): one affine lift sets each z to its incident X, each Y to its support sum and the four budget-only coordinates to 0; claim 1 adds the 2,150 source VarInt facts. Obligations 46,678 and 44,528 -- the two blocks differ only in the integrality flags, yet carry 91,206 of the certificate's 96,720 obligations.

Point claim: FiberStrictness{inclusion_claim:2}; values = the complete 20,617-coordinate source LP point (C18473=18/35, C18501=8/15, each incident edge 3/5, budget activity 22/21 <= 20); refutation = one Lin step over the target row R2035 (target index 821) plus its 22 cancelled observation fixings, deriving the constant 1/21 <= 0 and closing with Absurd.

The refutation is stated over the kernel-generated observation fiber: the 1,146 equalities a_i(x)=b_i(y) are appended in projection order and are never authored by the caller; strictness holds because no target point shares the projected source witness coordinates (docs/FORMAT_V6.md, 'Requested statement').

Removed-row justifications live only in the certificate: each of the 72 removed packing rows is proved from a retained superset row (71 strict supersets, 1 identical support), and the budget row is retained unchanged.
proof_encoding: RPA 6 text = exact 'RPA 6' header plus one compact JSON object {'claims':[3],'blocks':[3],'points':[1]}; one block per claim in order, each ending in {'Return':{'map':[20,617 affine expressions],'checks':[reference list]}}.

Expressions are {'constant':'str','terms':[[var_index,'str']]}; premises are index-addressed facts {'RowEq':i}, {'RowUpper':i}, {'VarLower':i}, {'VarUpper':i}, {'VarInt':i}, {'Local':j}, {'Assumption':k}. No symbolic names exist in the proof.

Block 0 holds 20,374 root steps: 18,467 alias Cases steps (each branch an EqPair of two Lin obligations), 1,000 Y-definition Lin steps, then packing/budget/objective Lin steps. All three blocks: 23,516 root steps, 1,848,760 linear terms, 172,177 substitution terms.

The point refutation is a separate fresh root block: one Lin step with an explicit constant field ('0') over 23 terms (the R2035 premise plus 22 observation-fixing facts addressed as RowEq index target_rows+j), closed by Absurd on the derived constant 1/21 <= 0.

Size is physical, not search: 39,845,824 B RPA / 30,500,427 B RPX for 96,720 obligations (~412 B each), all pattern-generated by hand-written dict assembly; the request (41,769 B) carries only the claim list and the point tag -- a 954x claim-to-proof ratio.
agent_manual_work: Wrote both MPS readers from scratch (token parser, then an independent fixed-field/Decimal scan) and used them as the only source of variable/row identities: no kernel readback of names, bounds or indices was used.

Established the saturation structure by exhaustive incidence analysis (18,467 edges, degree = |negative coefficient| on 1,146/1,146 rows, no repeated (X,Y) pair, one connected component) without any solver, relaxation solve or presolver.

Certified (by exact Fraction substitution, not sampling) that all 2,146 equalities collapse to 0=0, the budget row maps to sum(active X), and the objective maps to the new coefficients ranging -1,413 to -12; also verified 1,348 explicit assignments (1,199 feasible / 149 infeasible).

Constructed the strictness witness by hand as an exact rational point (3/5 on edges outside the shared neighborhood, X = incident sum / degree) and showed its projection violates retained row R2035 by exactly 1/21.

Still needed a second script to turn the audit into proof premises: tools/audit_test18.py rebuilds saturation groups, Y supports, superset witnesses, the reverse map and the fiber multipliers before a single RPA byte could be written.
preparer_helpers: tools/prepare_test18.py is 129 lines; imports inspect from audit_test18 (line 10), parse_mps,row_ref from prepare_affine (line 11), expression,plus,mul,expr_json,row_fact,substitute,sha from prepare_test40 (line 12) and Builder from prepare_test88 (line 13) -- 893 lines of sibling helpers under tools/.

prepare_test88.Builder (233 lines) is the de-facto proof API: alloc/refexpr/kind/lin/eqpair/cases, with hand-coded rule preconditions and assertions at tools/prepare_test88.py:35-43 and 47-56; ~20 sibling preparers import it.

prepare_affine.py re-implements MPS parsing (233 lines) with its own ordered variable ids, marker handling, RHS/RANGES/BOUNDS logic and range-aware row_ref, and is the index source for every numeric reference in the RPA.
prepare_test40.py:72-102 supplies the exact affine algebra (expression/plus/mul/expr_json/substitute/row_fact/facts/signature) from which the certificate JSON is assembled.

audit_test18.py:15-75 rebuilds the whole structure from the agent's 1.9 MB audit.json and emits the 4.3 MB projection_witness.json (reverse map for 20,617 coordinates, 1,146 saturation records, 1,000 Y records, 20,617-value source point, fiber multipliers) that prepare_test18 compiles into the RPA.
friction: Proof addressing is the compiler's problem: observation rows are referenced as RowEq at len(target_rows)+j (tools/prepare_test18.py:81) and every other premise by raw model-order index, so the preparer silently depends on rpx canonical preserving MPS declaration order.

Per-claim cost is invisible: verify reports one total work/obligations figure, and the preparer recomputes obligations_by_claim/root_steps_by_claim by hand (tools/prepare_test18.py:87-88) to see where the 96,720 obligations sit.

The five mutation receipts record only 'message' plus 'status' -- no code, no location -- so which rule each mutation broke cannot be recovered from the saved evidence (cases/test18/preparation.json:115-170).

One eval call failed: read('input/model.mps:raw') raised FileNotFoundError because ':raw' is a read-tool selector rather than a path (digest transcript, 1 of 16 tool calls failed), so the 1.6 MB MPS had to be re-read through a plain read().

The first assembled certificate returned RESOURCE_LIMIT 'proof work budget' at only 39.8 MB of the 256 MiB RPA limit: the binding budget was internal branch-state cost, so nothing in the artifact told the caller the proof was unaffordable (cases/test18/preparation.naive-resource-baseline.json:90).

notes: Trade-off answer: the claim is compact because it is an observational statement (1,146 coordinate pairs, three flag triples and one point tag = 41,769 B), while the proof is 954x larger because the kernel owns no lemma or template for the underlying pattern -- all 18,467 saturation identities must be re-derived from the raw model by local cases, so proof bytes and charged work scale with obligation count, not claim size. The API therefore owes the compiler: typed builders that make the 18,444-branch pattern generated rather than authored; a preflight/statistics report that attributes work, obligations, branches and peak live facts per claim and per point before assembly (these exact bytes were RESOURCE_LIMIT under whole-live-fact branch copies and VERIFIED at work 8,266,292 with 20,374 peak live facts afterwards, cases/test18/scope_replay.json:19); and a first-class way to bind a compact point claim to the kernel-generated fiber it refutes instead of naming synthetic rows as RowEq at target_rows+j. Scale: RPA 39,845,824 B, RPX 30,500,427 B, request 41,769 B, 23,516 root steps, 96,720 obligations, 18,444 branches, charged work 8,266,292 = 0.83% of the 1e9 default, peak live facts 20,374 = 2.0% of the 1e6 limit, execute 946 ms (cases/test18/scope_replay.json:19).
